newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends lower after late sell-off.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends lower after late sell-off.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures spun to weaker close late Friday after a shortcovering rally ran out of steam, trading sources said.

Prices nudged up against nearby resistance throughout the day, but trade-linked selling prevented the market from scoring more convincing gains. When the May contract appeared stalled at $1,344 a tonne, speculators scrambled to liquidate their longs before the close.
May futures closed $5 lower at $1,325 after trading from $1,321 to $1,344. July fell $7 to $1,348.
Today's performance suggests the market may lack the strength to prolong its recent move to one-month highs, said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast.
"It is basically signaling that the short-covering rally is over with and that the market will correct," she said. "The bearish move is over with, but it may not have the momentum to go higher."
A fall through $1,316 basis May would likely trigger aggressive speculative selling, she said, with $1,300 seen as the next support level.
An estimated 10,093 lots changed hands on the day, more than double Thursday's official total of 4,066.
In other news, global cocoa consumption should increase by three to four percent annually over the next five years, a leading cocoa analyst said on Friday.

Global consumption could grow by 20 percent by 2002, Stephen Wateridge, the head of research at E.D. & F. Man, said in remarks to the Cocoa Merchants Association's conference in Phoenix, Arizona. ((-- W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
